key_insight: Deep Koopman Sensing is a reduced-order data-assimilation framework that reconstructs fluid flows from sparse sensors better than standard learned surrogates, because it is designed for the estimation task rather than only for forecasting.
engineering_relevance: It enables real-time flow state estimation for CFD applications such as monitoring and control when full first-principles simulation is too expensive.
method: Nonlinear autoencoder maps flow fields to a compact latent state.
Parameter-conditioned linear latent dynamics approximate the Koopman operator in latent space.
State estimation is performed with Kalman-style filtering using sparse sensor measurements.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on four benchmarks—1D Burgers, 2D cylinder flow, 2D dambreak, and 3D sphere flow—the Koopman model achieved the lowest assimilation error, and sensor updates helped linear latent models but could degrade nonlinear ones under EKF.
watch_item: Performance depends on the choice of filter and latent model; strong open-loop forecast accuracy does not guarantee good assimilation, so online robustness must be tested explicitly.
